about.title: Personal Injury Help in Martinez, California
about.longDescription: Martinez sits along busy corridors like Alhambra Avenue, SR-4, and I-680, where daily commuter and local traffic mix. In the most recent full year on record, the city logged 116 injury collisions, 141 people injured, and 2 traffic deaths — numbers that reflect how often ordinary trips can turn into something life-changing. If you were hurt in a collision on one of these roads, or in a fall, workplace incident, or other accident anywhere in Martinez, you likely have questions about what comes next: medical bills, missed work, insurance calls that don't feel fair. We handle personal injury claims and offer free case reviews to injured people in Martinez and throughout Contra Costa County. Our team will look at what happened and explain your options. There's no upfront cost, and we only get paid if you recover compensation. If something happened to you in Martinez, it costs nothing to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Decide

items.title: You Have Two Years — But Don't Wait
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Talking to us early helps make sure no deadline slips by.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't Shut the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so the value of a claim isn't artificially limited.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning legal fees only come out of money recovered for you — there's no bill if there's no payout.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer free case reviews. If you decide to move forward, we work on contingency, so you don't pay unless you recover compensation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an accident in Martinez?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. If a government entity was involved — like a city road issue — the window can be much shorter, sometimes just six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you were partially at fault. Your share of responsibility would reduce, not eliminate, what you might receive.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Martinez?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher volumes along corridors such as Alhambra Avenue, SR-4, and I-680, with reported crashes tending to peak on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m. These are simply recorded counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Do you handle personal injury cases?
items.answer: Yes. We handle personal injury claims throughout Martinez and Contra Costa County. Our team can review what happened to you and explain your legal options during a free case consultation. We work on contingency, so you only pay if you recover.
